name.description: The immutable name of the Queued Resource.
name.rationale: This argument identifies the Queued Resource and does not directly affect access control, networking, or security posture.

zone.description: The GCP location for the Queued Resource. If it is not provided, the provider zone is used.
zone.rationale: Zone controls where the Queued Resource is deployed. Restricting deployment to approved Australia regions supports data residency, governance, and organisational security requirements.

project.description: If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project identifies where the Queued Resource is created. It is required for resource placement but does not directly define the security behaviour checked by these policies.

tpu.rationale: This block defines the TPU resource configuration. Security impact is assessed at the nested attribute level.

tpu.node_spec.rationale: This block specifies the TPU node configuration. Security impact is assessed at the nested attribute level.

node_spec.rationale: This block specifies node configuration. Security impact is assessed at the nested attribute level.

node_spec.parent.rationale: This argument identifies the parent resource location and does not directly affect the security posture of the Queued Resource.

node_spec.node_id.description: Unqualified node identifier used to identify the node in the project once provisioned.
node_spec.node_id.rationale: This argument is used for identification purposes only and does not affect access control or network exposure.

node_spec.node.rationale: This block defines the node settings. Security impact is assessed at the nested attribute level.

node.rationale: This block defines the TPU node settings. Security impact is assessed at the nested attribute level.

node.runtime_version.rationale: This argument controls the TPU runtime version. It may affect compatibility but is not directly used as a security control.

node.accelerator_type.description: TPU accelerator type for the TPU. If not specified, this defaults to 'v2-8'.
node.accelerator_type.rationale: This argument controls TPU hardware capacity and performance rather than the security posture of the Queued Resource.

node.description.rationale: This argument is only descriptive metadata and does not directly affect access control, networking, or security.

node.network_config.description: Network configurations for the TPU node.
node.network_config.rationale: Network configuration controls whether the TPU worker is exposed to the public internet and whether IP forwarding is enabled. Misconfiguration can increase the attack surface.

network_config.description: Network configurations for the TPU node.
network_config.rationale: Network configuration controls whether the TPU worker is exposed to the public internet and whether IP forwarding is enabled. Misconfiguration can increase the attack surface.

network_config.network.description: The name of the network for the TPU node. If none is provided, default will be used.
network_config.network.rationale: This argument selects the VPC network. The security impact is mainly determined by exposure settings such as external IPs and IP forwarding, not the network name itself.

network_config.subnetwork.description: The name of the subnetwork for the TPU node. If none is provided, default will be used.
network_config.subnetwork.rationale: This argument selects the subnetwork. The security impact is mainly determined by whether external IPs and IP forwarding are enabled.

network_config.enable_external_ips.description: Indicates that external IP addresses would be associated with the TPU workers. If set to false, the subnetwork should have Private Google Access enabled.
network_config.enable_external_ips.rationale: Enabling external IPs exposes the TPU worker directly to the public internet, increasing the attack surface. TPU workloads should use internal IPs with Private Google Access enabled.

network_config.can_ip_forward.description: Allows the TPU node to send and receive packets with non-matching destination or source IPs.
network_config.can_ip_forward.rationale: Enabling can_ip_forward allows the TPU node to send and receive packets with non-matching source or destination IPs, which can increase the attack surface by enabling spoofing or unintended routing.

network_config.queue_count.description: Specifies networking queue count for TPU VM instance's network interface.
network_config.queue_count.rationale: This argument controls network performance tuning and does not directly affect the security posture of the Queued Resource.
